principles: Prefer developer continuity when host capacity is unavailable.
Make degraded review visible to users, gates, and audits.
drivers: Second host credit/auth/runtime failures should not indefinitely block ordinary development.
The fallback must not be misrepresented as independent two-host review.
Follow-up implementation needs precise artifacts, commands, and tests.

options.name: A: Strict 3x2 only
cons: Can block development when another host is out of credits, unauthenticated, or unavailable
Poor practical fallback for solo/local users

options.name: B: Silent downgrade to 3x1
pros: Keeps development moving with minimal UX friction
cons: Undermines the purpose of two-host review

options.name: C: Explicit degraded 3x1 fallback
pros: Allows progress when a second host cannot run
Records degraded reason and assurance level
Supports stricter tests and audit visibility
cons: Still weaker than true two-host independence

rationale: Choose explicit degraded 3x1 fallback because it solves the user capacity problem without claiming false two-host independence. The plan should require unavailable-host reason codes, degraded artifacts, stronger local evidence, and clear limits.

preMortem.scenario: Teams start using degraded 3x1 as the normal path.
preMortem.trigger: The fallback is automatic and invisible.
preMortem.consequence: The project loses the independent-review guarantee while reports still look like strong review.
preMortem.mitigation: Require explicit unavailable-host reason codes, degradedQuorum=true, and separate status text that never says full 3x2 passed.

preMortem.scenario: High-risk changes ship with weak review.
preMortem.trigger: A second host is unavailable during a risky gate or decision-doc change.
preMortem.consequence: Important process or safety changes receive only single-host scrutiny.
preMortem.mitigation: Document policy limits: default remains 3x2, degraded path must be visible and can require user/project approval for high-risk classes.

preMortem.scenario: Implementation treats any host error as fallback eligibility.
preMortem.trigger: The code accepts vague failure text instead of structured host availability evidence.
preMortem.consequence: Developers can bypass two-host review for convenience.
preMortem.mitigation: Require structured reason codes and recent host_runtime/credit/auth evidence, plus negative controls for fabricated unavailability.
